subject: Proposal: dedicated GPU footprint and commit tiers for Acme Health
messages:
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: initial workload details & ask

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this. We’re evaluating a dedicated GPU pool for our consumer-facing conversational assistant and procurement asked me to get concrete sizing and committed pricing options. Quick snapshot of our workload: 
- Avg monthly active users: ~420k
- Avg requests/day: 400k (roughly 12M/month)
- Typical request: prompt 1024 tokens, response 512 tokens (chat + retrieval-enhanced generation mix)
- Peak concurrency: 250 qps sustained for 15–20 minute spikes; base concurrency ~60 qps
- Latency target: 95p < 400ms for short-turn queries, < 750ms for long form
- Context/cache: ~60% of calls hit the prefix cache; 40% cold KV cache
- Reliability: HIPAA-adjacent workloads — will need Private or Dedicated with SOC2 + VPC peering

What we need from Redwood: recommended pool size (GPU type options), throughput guarantees, pricing for 12- and 24-month reserved commits, and any suggested configuration (autoscale/burst capacity, warm standbys). I attached a small sample of request logs.

Also open to a phased approach: short pilot, then full commit. Can you come back with a few capacity tiers and price bands?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Rivera
Head of Product, Acme Health
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial workload details & ask

Tom — thanks for the detail, this is very helpful. I shared the sample with Solutions and Pricing; a couple quick clarifying items before we size: 
1) For the 250 qps peak, is that measured at application-level (after frontend batching) or raw model requests?
2) How often do you see >1k-token prompts vs shorter ones? Any percentiles (p50/p95) for prompt+response length?
3) Are you expecting session affinity (long-lived KV caches per user) that would push memory requirements per replica?

Initial thoughts: given your token mix and the cold-rate, we’ll likely recommend a mix of H100-equivalent for hot-path low-latency routing and A100-80GB for cost-efficient batch handling for background jobs. I’ll pull an initial throughput model and a few commit tiers (12/24mo) and get back with concrete GPU counts and suggested guarantees.

I’m attaching the workload sample we received. We’ll aim to have a first-pass proposal by early next week.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial workload details & ask

Hi Soojin — quick answers: 
- 250 qps is at the call level to the model (we do minimal frontend batching)
- Token percentiles (prompt + response): p50 ~ 900 tokens, p95 ~ 1600 tokens
- We use session affinity for certain long-running conversations but the active working set per replica is small (~2–4 users max); most is prefix caching

We’re fine with a mixed fleet if Redwood recommends it. The main tradeoff for us is price vs guaranteed throughput — procurement will push for a clear committed baseline with credits for overage. Happy to take a phased 2–3 week canary.

Tom
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood recommended footprint and commit tiers for Acme Health (first pass)

Tom / Priya — thanks for the extra info. Below is a concise first-pass recommendation and pricing bands. Numbers are conservative with 15% headroom for autoscaling and maintenance.

Workload assumptions (from your data):
- Monthly tokens (approx): 12M requests * (avg 1200 tokens) = ~14.4B tokens/month
- Effective tokens/sec at peak (250 qps * 1200 tokens * 1/second) = 300k tokens/sec sustained during spikes
- Cold-rate affecting latency: 40% cold generates KV-loads and slightly higher per-token compute

Recommended pool (phase 1):
- Hot tier: 6 x H100 (or equivalent) for low-latency routing (95p target ~250–400ms on p50 short calls)
- Batch/efficiency tier: 8 x A100-80GB for throughput and batchable work (background summarization/rerank)
- Warm standbys: 2 GPUs (mix) to handle failures and fast bursts
- Total active GPUs: 14 (plus 2 warm) — we estimate this covers sustained base + 15% headroom and 20% expected batch consolidation.

Throughput guarantees & SLOs (example):
- Baseline commit: 95% of requests served within configured p95 latency targets (short: <=400ms, long: <=750ms)
- Burst protection: guaranteed handling up to 300 qps for 10 minutes without scaling penalties (uses burst buffer & warm standbys)

Pricing / commit bands (illustrative):
- 12-month reserved commit: 18% discount off list host pricing + $X/month per H100-equivalent + $Y/month per A100-equivalent
- 24-month reserved commit: 27% discount + additional commit credits for overages at reduced rate (applies after baseline)
- Pilot (30 days): limited credits (equivalent to ~1 GPU-month) and option to convert to reserved commit within 45 days with pricing protection.

Example cost math (very rough):
- Estimate token unit cost on dedicated baseline = $0.00012 / 1k tokens (after commit discount)
- For 14.4B tokens/month -> ~$1,728 baseline pricing before reserved commit credits and infra adjustments

Notes on variability and options:
- If you can accept slightly higher p95 for long calls, we can shift 2 H100 -> A100 to reduce cost (~8–10% savings).
- We recommend a rebaseline clause at 90 days to reconcile actual utilization and adjust the pool or credits.
- Security/compliance: Private routing + VPC peering and SOC2 logs are standard for Dedicated customers; we’ll include audit retention options in the LOI.

I attached a detailed SKU/pricing workbook and a commit-tier summary PDF. Happy to walk through the math with your procurement team.

— Rishi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood recommended footprint and commit tiers for Acme Health (first pass)

Rishi — thanks for the detailed breakdown. Procurement has three asks: 
1) Can Acme get an incremental discount if we commit to a 36-month term?
2) We need a firm overage credit policy (how many tokens convert to credits, or monetary offsets?)
3) For the pilot, can Redwood provide a dedicated canary with identical topology (not shared), and a defined rollback clause if latency targets aren’t met?

Also, the $X/$Y placeholders need concrete numbers for us to run through our internal approval spreadsheet. Can you replace with actual per-GPU/month figures?

Priya
Acme Health — Procurement
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps & LOI path forward

Priya / Tom — great questions. Quick answers and next steps: 
- 36-month option: we can propose a 36-month band with an incremental ~4% additional discount on top of the 24-month figure, subject to minimum spend thresholds. I’ll get exact numbers into the pricing workbook by Monday.
- Overage credits: we propose a two-tier overage policy: 1) monthly token overages up to 10% are converted to dollar credits at the committed rate; 2) beyond 10% becomes billable at the reduced overage rate defined in the contract. We’ll put concrete rates in the LOI.
- Pilot canary: we can provide a dedicated canary topology identical to the proposed active pool for a 21-day pilot. If p95 latency targets aren’t met for 3 consecutive days during the pilot, you can elect a rollback or get a proportional credit.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Update the pricing workbook with per-GPU/month dollar figures (H100 / A100 unit rates) and the 36-month option.
2) Draft LOI with pilot terms, rollback clause, and rebaseline at 90 days.
3) Send DocuSign LOI and a HubSpot deal link for signature and procurement tracking.

We’ll include the SKU workbook and LOI draft in the next email. If procurement is ready, I’ll loop legal and engineering to schedule a 30-min pricing review next Tuesday.

Thanks — speak soon.
— Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: workload_samples.csv (redacted), redwood-dedicated-sku-pricing.xlsx, commit-tier-summary.pdf, DocuSign-Acme-LOI.pdf
